The **International Society of Thrombosis and Hemostasis (ISTH)** is a global medical organization whose clinical criteria serve as a foundational standard for evaluating patient safety in the Danish healthcare system. Within the context of the Danish national quality indicators for [[atrieflimren|atrieflimren]] (atrial fibrillation), adapted ISTH criteria are utilized to strictly define and measure [[alvorlig-bloedning|Alvorlig blødning]] (major bleeding) [^src2]. 

The organization's primary significance in this corpus is its direct relationship with [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]], a key quality metric that tracks the incidence of major bleeding among prevalent atrial fibrillation patients [^src1]. By applying adapted ISTH criteria, Danish health authorities ensure that the measurement of severe bleeding events—including critical outcomes such as [[intrakraniel-bloedning|Intrakraniel blødning]] (intracranial bleeding)—is standardized and internationally comparable [^src2]. This methodological alignment allows the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) and the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute to systematically monitor the safety of anticoagulation therapies across national, regional, and local levels [^src5]. 

Notably, while [[indikator-7|Indikator 7]] does not have a predefined numerical standard or target threshold to achieve, it relies entirely on the adapted ISTH criteria to report incidence rates and evaluate clinical quality over time [^src1]. The consistent use of these criteria across multiple annual reports (from 2023 to 2025) underscores the ISTH's role as the authoritative reference for defining bleeding complications in Danish cardiovascular quality assurance [^src3], [^src6].
